Execution discipline

  • Every task begins with its requirements and current source references. New public types/APIs in the plan are labeled proposed.
  • Entry click counts are target budgets from the owning page, not measured runtime results. Preparing data and necessary safety review are not equivalent to discovering a tool.
  • Do not hardcode a Figma example ID, quantity, sequence or computed result in production.
  • Do not interpret every Figma frame as a route or every success-content example as a modal.
  • Current-code observations, target requirements and unverified runtime behavior remain distinct.
  • Update traceability with actual commit/test evidence; checkboxes alone are not proof.
  • No source application code was changed or scientific tests run to create this specification.

Product scope and implementation authority

Product scope and implementation authority

Product

HelixBench is a local-first, offline Windows molecular-biology workbench in Rust. The existing native GPUI shell renders a framework-independent appcore over domain and storage. Primary users import, inspect, edit and analyze sequences; lab records connect scientific identity, experimental notes and physical samples.

Implementation authority

The user selected UX v4 as the target while preserving existing scientific capabilities. Apply this specification as the interaction contract, Figma as visual/flow evidence, and the inspected code as the current behavior/API baseline. Existing DESIGN.md describes the older palette/type/layout and must be reconciled in the implementation PR rather than silently treated as the new visual authority.

Read in order

Start with README.md, this chapter, shared contracts, data/migrations, screen chapters and the implementation plan. Before each task read its feature IDs, relevant state-machine transitions, current code references and acceptance cases. Update the traceability registry and tests with every completed slice.

State versus screen

There are 19 primary module pages and 686 Figma root frames in the captured v4 page. Frames include forms, reference material, duplicate responsive variants and scenario-specific states. Do not create 686 production routes or hardcode the text/IDs/numbers in these examples. Use typed state, a shared shell and reusable renderers.

Local review and requests

Existing review events have actor strings and local statuses. A local review/request transition is not authenticated remote delivery. Use local workflow copy until a separately scoped service, account model, permissions and delivery protocol exist. Reviewer A is a prototype persona.

Baseline

Repository revision: 0474cb94e456094dc4e501a9351ca7587a149361. The working tree was clean at inspection. The reference index captures 82 Rust files, 35,137 Rust lines, 1,133 function declarations, 218 struct/enum declarations and 181 test functions. These are static inspection counts; no application or scientific test suite was executed for this documentation task.

Completeness boundary

The bundle catalogs the existing curated 212 feature entries, 25 explicit UX additions, all 19 primary screens, all captured Figma frame content/actions and the inspected source API/types. Runtime scientific validity, keyboard/assistive-technology behavior, persistence fault handling and user task performance require implementation/testing. Prototype links are not proof of these behaviors.

Decision register

DEC-01 · Authority

Status: Accepted by user

UX v4 defines target interaction and visual behavior. Existing scientific capabilities are preserved; code/schema evidence controls what currently exists. Prototype fixtures never define actual numerical results.

DEC-02 · Runtime

Status: Baseline constraint

Keep the Rust 2021 workspace, native GPUI shell and domain/appcore/storage boundaries. Do not replace the UI with a web shell or egui.

DEC-03 · Local workflow

Status: Target default from existing product

Remain local-first, offline and account-free. Review/request/audience states are local workflow records. Real remote delivery, authentication and multi-user authorization require a separate approved scope.

DEC-04 · Molecular typing

Status: Target policy

Keep DnaSequence as DNA. Route RNA/oligo and protein inputs through explicit typed representations/module handoffs. Until a molecule can be represented safely, block its commit with original input retained; never clean protein into DNA.

DEC-05 · Stable identity

Status: Proposed engineering decision

Add UUID-backed document/revision/result/operation identities while preserving existing store-local u64 keys. Persist identities once; importing as a copy remints document identity and retains original provenance.

DEC-06 · Deletion

Status: Target policy resolving example ambiguity

Block active live dependencies and historical outputs lacking an immutable input snapshot. A historical result with complete provenance may retain a tombstone after source deletion. Archive is the safe default.

DEC-07 · Version retention

Status: Target policy

Retain the current checkpoint behavior for unreferenced history, but pin or separately snapshot every source used by a retained result. The current 20-checkpoint cap cannot break provenance.

DEC-08 · Operation semantics

Status: Target policy

Compute from an immutable captured input; validate before writeback; persist a recoverable operation journal for cross-store mutations. Offer cancellation only at a supported stage.

DEC-09 · Two-click measure

Status: Accepted by user

Feature entry is within two navigation clicks from its owning page. Labeled page navigation is one click. Data entry, OS file picking and necessary safety confirmation are measured separately.

DEC-10 · Presentation

Status: Target policy

Use one persistent shell, contextual right panel, modal decisions for consequential operations and inline/toast completion for routine actions. Figma feedback-content frames are not instructions to build hundreds of blocking modals.

DEC-11 · Schema compatibility

Status: Proposed engineering decision

Introduce native schema v2 for durable identities/provenance. Read v1, migrate in memory and save only on explicit user action, with a recoverable backup. Newer unsupported versions remain read-protected and explain the required app update.

DEC-12 · Scientific claims

Status: Release gate

Use engine-specific method names and disclose implemented limitations. CRISPR scores are local Rule-Set-2-style/CFD implementations, local BLAST is a seed-and-extend search, and chemistry supports a SMILES subset. Independent method validation precedes stronger scientific claims.

Shared interaction contracts

Shared interaction contracts

Persistent shell

Maintain labeled navigation, document identity, draft/saved state, document tabs, current scientific view, task content and the contextual right panel. Use the existing GPUI hierarchy; do not render product functions as disconnected pages because a Figma example was an isolated frame.

Command discovery

Create a single command registry with ID, visible label, owning page, category, input requirements, availability reason, shortcut and typed action. The owning page exposes its common tools directly and the complete catalog in one click; choosing the tool is the second click. Avoid an additional Advanced submenu that adds a third discovery click.

Input/selection context

Capture document/revision, selected range/strand, active split pane, selected feature/primer IDs, typed entity reference and plate/well set in the command context. A tool opened from another module explicitly asks which input to use. If that input disappears, show a prerequisite/recovery state; never substitute another record.

Navigation and dirty guards

Keep view switches and read-only tools inside the same draft without a guard. Guard only an intent that would discard/replace data or cannot preserve the draft: document/app close, destructive replacement and relevant file/document transitions. Save performs the exact pending intent only after successful persistence. Discard restores the saved source before continuing. Stay/Escape returns to the invoking view with input retained.

Back and return

Store a typed ReturnLocation with route, source IDs, scope/query, filters/sort, selection and scroll anchor. Back is not a hardcoded Home button. An explicit Back to search returns to the same search scope/query; a source link opens the historical revision when that is what the result references.

Forms

Separate draft values from committed objects. Define required fields, valid formats/ranges, inline errors and submit availability. Repeated submits are idempotent at the application operation boundary. Preserve user input on validation/write failure. Cancel has no mutation. When an input changes, clear or mark stale any computed preview.

Feedback

Use inline field errors for correctable input, inline page status/toast for routine success and modal decisions for consequential choices. Every message names the affected object, outcome and constructive next action. Do not implement every operation-outcome frame as a blocking confirmation. Status is announced without moving focus unnecessarily.

Empty-state taxonomy

Distinguish no records yet, no matching query, no rows after filters, no scientific matches, processing, failed load, inaccessible source and restricted/locked action. Give a relevant creation/reset/retry/locate remedy. Cave-art illustration remains decorative and must not carry the only explanation or obscure the primary action.

Tables and grids

Rows and cells act on stable identities; sort/filter never retargets a mutation. A colored row is a real selected/hover state, not a misleading decorative default. After deletion, clear the inspector and row selection unless an explicit next-record selection is made. Virtualize large tables and provide keyboard activation.

Units and coordinates

Show quantity dimension and unit with every numeric value. Validate finite numbers before calculation. UI positions are 1-based inclusive; internal ranges are zero-based start plus length. Circular origin wrapping is an explicit representation, not an invalid negative-length interval.

Modal versus panel

Specify each surface as non-modal inspector, modal dialog, popover, toast or full task view. A modal has initial focus, contained tab order, inert background, Escape/cancel and logical focus return. A non-modal panel permits keyboard movement back to the workspace and has an explicit Close control.

Responsive behavior

Use fluid GPUI layout. At 1280px, preserve usable main content and open the right panel on demand; do not scale all text and controls down. At wider widths, panel pinning is available. Wrap header actions, use accessible horizontal table scrolling and keep focused controls visible at increased Windows DPI/text size. The captured 1280 cohort is evidence for named first-use paths, not every possible layout.

Keyboard contract

Preserve Ctrl+N/O/S, Ctrl+Shift+S, Ctrl+Z/Y, Ctrl+F, Escape, Ctrl+A/C/X/V, Delete/Backspace and Ctrl+1–6 as inspected. Text inputs consume editing keys before global sequence shortcuts. Add global workspace Search as a separate command (proposed Ctrl+K); Ctrl+F continues to search the active sequence. Focus ring and error examples appear in the interaction-contract Figma frame.

Sample mode

Sample records have an explicit origin and namespace throughout setup/results. Exiting keeps them separate from personal records. Saving a personal copy allocates a new document ID/revision and retains source attribution; sample result IDs are never relabeled as personal analysis outputs.

Non-negotiable invariants

INV-01 · Typed identity

Every command carries stable source/target IDs and relevant revision IDs. Never bind a mutation to a display name, row index or currently active record at completion time.

INV-02 · Coordinate contract

UI coordinates are 1-based inclusive. Domain Range is zero-based start plus length, with documented circular wrap. Conversions occur at a typed boundary and are tested once.

INV-03 · Preserve input

Keep original import/paste text and produce a transformation report before meaningful changes. Invalid input cannot silently disappear.

INV-04 · No silent substitution

A protein tool cannot choose a chain because DNA is active; a well cannot become A1 because H12 was clicked; no selection yields a prerequisite state.

INV-05 · Draft safety

View switches retain the same draft. Destructive replacement, document close, file open and app close guard dirty data. Save failure/cancel never performs the pending intent.

INV-06 · Saved truth

The UI reports saved/submitted/deleted only after the required persistence boundary succeeds. Partial/uncertain outcomes are not called success.

INV-07 · Historical truth

Result, submitted-entry and plate-snapshot provenance is immutable. New source edits do not rewrite old outputs.

INV-08 · Selection truth

Deleting a selection clears its inspector and actions. Filters/sorts retain the selected ID or explicitly clear it; they never select an unrelated row silently.

INV-09 · Async truth

Each job has an operation ID and captured inputs. Closing a view does not retarget its completion; stale results remain tied to their captured source.

INV-10 · Local truth

The local application does not claim remote delivery, authenticated review or cloud synchronization without an implemented service.

INV-11 · Recoverable mutation

Multi-record and cross-store actions validate a complete plan, commit predictably, and reconcile on restart without repeating successful writes.

INV-12 · Accessible operation

Visible labels, focus, keyboard navigation, readable scientific alternatives and announced status are part of the interaction, not optional decoration.

Data, state and persistence contracts

Data, state and persistence contracts

Current architecture

domain owns scientific/domain types; storage owns local formats and persistence; appcore owns application actions/state and orchestrates work; desktop_gpui renders and dispatches. Keep algorithms headlessly testable. Existing AppState has an active Document plus OpenDoc library entries and several independent local stores.

Identity gaps

Current Document has name, sequence, features, primers and version snapshots but no durable document/revision ID. Registry links documents by name; Inventory links an entity using Option<String>. Introduce typed durable references and migrate name links only when resolution is unique. Preserve unresolved/ambiguous legacy links for user repair rather than selecting the first name match.

Proposed identity types

Introduce DocumentId, RevisionId, ResultId and OperationId as UUID-backed opaque newtypes. Keep existing u64 IDs within their store and wrap cross-store references with a StoreKind discriminator. Display aliases such as DNA-001 are labels and fixtures, not primary keys. New copies get new identities; reopening the same native document preserves identity.

Revision and result

AnalysisResult stores tool/method version, immutable typed input references/snapshots, captured selection/topology/units, validated parameters, timestamps, output payload, persistence status and optional current-source comparison. A draft analysis captures a durable draft snapshot; do not call it saved version 7 if it contains unsaved edits.

Selection and route

SelectionContext is independent of the renderer. Route/ReturnLocation carry typed targets, queries and view state. A pending operation stores the exact original context; completion never reads a newly active document as its input.

Native-file v2 migration

Read current v1 files, allocate durable IDs once during migration, retain feature/primer IDs, and migrate version snapshots to stable revision references. Save as native v2 only on explicit user save, with a recoverable original backup and a compatibility explanation. Unknown newer format versions are not overwritten. Preserve original input bytes until migration/interpretation review completes.

Cross-store journal

Per-file atomic rename is not a multi-store transaction. For result submission, transfers and automation writeback, persist an operation plan with unique operation/output IDs and preconditions, write staged changes, atomically advance commit markers and reconcile incomplete journals at restart. Recovery must determine already committed outputs before retrying.

Atomic save

Keep the existing atomic-write behavior but use operation-unique sibling temp names and serialize competing writes to the same destination. Flush/sync before replace. On failure, preserve the last good file, keep the document dirty and show a recoverable error. Propagate ignored storage errors back to the action result rather than showing success.

Runtime operation states

Separate the existing domain RunStatus (Completed/Failed) from a richer operation controller: Reviewing, Queued, Running, CancelRequested, Canceled, Completed, Failed and PartialOutcome. Stage-specific cancellation must be truthful. A job works from a captured immutable input and dispatches completion to the UI through its operation ID.

Dependency and tombstone policy

Archive is reversible and removes a record from active views. Permanent deletion blocks active live dependencies and historical results that cannot retain their inputs. Fully snapshotted historical results may retain an unavailable-source tombstone. Revalidate dependencies immediately before commit; after success clear active selection/actions and invalidate search caches.

Local review revisions

Preserve current EntryStatus values and local ReviewEvent data. Add immutable submitted revision snapshots and distinguish author draft from the submitted revision. A review revision is read-only even though an independently edited draft may be allowed; never mutate a reviewer’s frozen input in place.

Inventory migration

Existing quantities are f32 plus a unit string; concentration lacks an explicit unit. Normalize recognized quantity unit spellings, retain raw legacy values and mark unknown concentration units unresolved. Do not infer ng/µL or assign sample fixture values to real records. New transfer calculations use dimensioned validated values and explicit conversion.

Scientific persistence

Retain outputs by source revision and method. Older results remain valid historical observations even if the current input changed; label them older-input, offer rerun with a new result ID and preserve the previous output. Pin source snapshots independently of the existing 20-checkpoint retention cap.

Proposed interfaces

All names below are proposed contracts, not assertions about installed APIs. Introduce supporting types in the owning task and retain adapters for current call sites until migrated.

// PROPOSED interfaces; these do not exist in the baseline code.
pub struct SourceRef { pub document: DocumentId, pub revision: RevisionId }
pub struct RecordRef { pub store: StoreKind, pub local_id: u64 }
pub struct WellRef { pub plate_id: u64, pub coordinate: WellCoordinate }
pub struct SelectionContext {
    pub source: Option<SourceRef>, pub range: Option<domain::Range>,
    pub strand: domain::sequence::Strand, pub active_pane: PaneId,
    pub records: Vec<RecordRef>, pub wells: Vec<WellRef>,
}
pub struct ReturnLocation { pub route: Route, pub query: Option<SearchQuery>, pub view: ViewState }
pub enum NavigationIntent {
    Navigate(Route), OpenFile(std::path::PathBuf), SwitchDocument(DocumentId),
    CloseDocument(DocumentId), ExitApplication,
}
pub fn request_navigation(state: &mut AppState, intent: NavigationIntent) -> NavigationOutcome;
pub fn resolve_guard(state: &mut AppState, decision: GuardDecision) -> Result<NavigationOutcome, AppError>;
pub fn preview_import(source: ImportSource, options: ImportOptions) -> Result<ImportPreview, ImportError>;
pub fn commit_import(state: &mut AppState, plan: ReviewedImportPlan) -> Result<Vec<DocumentId>, AppError>;
pub fn dispatch_command(state: &mut AppState, id: CommandId, context: SelectionContext) -> Result<CommandOutcome, AppError>;
pub fn start_analysis(input: CapturedInput, parameters: AnalysisParameters) -> Result<OperationId, AppError>;
pub fn save_analysis(result: AnalysisResult, destination: ResultDestination) -> Result<ResultId, StorageError>;
pub fn plan_transfer(inventory: &Inventory, request: TransferRequest) -> Result<TransferPlan, Vec<FieldError>>;
pub fn commit_transfer(plan: ReviewedTransferPlan, stores: &mut WorkspaceStores) -> Result<OperationReceipt, AppError>;
pub fn reconcile_operation(id: OperationId, stores: &mut WorkspaceStores) -> Result<RecoveryPlan, AppError>;

Proposed dependency policy

UUID v4/serde support is documented by the uuid crate. SHA-256 is documented by RustCrypto sha2. Proposed versions are uuid 1.29.2 with v4/serde and sha2 0.11.1; verify installed-toolchain/MSRV compatibility before adding them and commit the lockfile. Keep UI aliases separate from opaque IDs. A canonical versioned input digest includes algorithm-relevant sequence/type/topology, scope/strand, primer or chain data and ordered parameters; it never replaces the durable source revision reference.

Verified code-to-target gaps

Verified code-to-target gaps

Import cleaning

storage::fasta::parse_all builds Document::from_sequence_text; clean_sequence uppercases supported characters, converts U to T and filters unsupported symbols. load_any uses parse_first for FASTA. Add interpretation/validation reporting before these mutation-producing paths; offer all records and never silently clean protein/RNA into DNA.

Stable source identity

Document/Version do not currently supply durable IDs; Registry.linked_doc and Inventory.entity use names/strings. Figma source identity must become typed persisted data, not a UI-only string.

Result lifecycle

Existing cached Analysis and saved alignments are not a general durable catalog for all tool results. Add a result store with source snapshots, method/parameters, stale-input comparison and refind routes. Preserve the existing reloadable alignment behavior.

Dirty intent coverage

PendingAction currently covers CloseApp, NewDemo, NewEmpty, Open and OpenRecent. Extend the typed intent/return model for document close/switch and relevant replacement operations; preserve existing dirty history semantics.

Notebook locking

Entry::locked currently locks Approved/Archived. The target requires a read-only submitted revision snapshot, not blanket mutation of the same in-review Entry data. Row submission is presently represented by a table-level submitted flag; target per-row outcomes need stable submitted-result identities.

Registry union

Registry::Kind contains Plasmid, Strain and Primer. Figma protein/RNA rows require a typed federated view over the specialist stores or an explicit schema extension/migration, not arbitrary Kind indexes.

Inventory transfer

Current Inventory has add/place/set_contents/fill_wells/snapshot but no validated transactional transfer API. fill_wells appends children without comprehensive collision/unit validation. Implement explicit reviewed assignment/transfer plans and snapshot-preserving commit behavior.

Automation state

Current RunStatus is Completed/Failed and Run lacks a durable source/template revision/writeback ledger. Running/cancel/partial/recovery screens require new state and persistence, not only UI branches.

Automation destination bug

Current appcore::automation_run registers rows with a Name column as plasmids after a Completed run and ignores save results. It does not adequately dispatch writeback according to OutputRegistry versus OutputResults. Add tests proving output-target isolation, truthful persistence success and idempotent recovery.

CSV semantics

The inspected automation execution uses line and comma splitting. Replace ingestion with a quoting-aware parser at the storage/appcore boundary and pass a typed table into domain execution. Preserve supported existing pipelines and reject malformed input before writeback.

Scoring claims

CRISPR code comments describe heuristic/Rule-Set-2-style scoring; chemistry explicitly supports a SMILES subset. Preserve computations but document actual method coverage and tests. Do not promote UI labels into claims of equivalence with validated external tools.

Theme baseline

Existing DESIGN.md and theme.rs use older tokens, system typography and tighter layout. UX v4 uses Soft Gallery foundations and a contextual right panel. Centralize the new token mapping while retaining semantic feature colors and high-density scientific views.

Prototype versus code

The 686-frame state catalog documents authored examples. A matching prototype link does not mean a schema, command, result store, file export, cancellation mechanism or authenticated reviewer already exists. Feature status in the traceability registry is explicitly scoped.

Functional state machines and transitions

Functional state machines and transitions

Import

Idle → SourceChosen → Parsing → ReviewReady or ReviewIssues → Correcting/Selection/DuplicateDecision → Committing → Opened or CommitFailed. No parse review commits data. Cancel returns to the source task with existing documents intact. Partial import explicitly records accepted/rejected records and preserves their original order/index.

Document draft

Clean → Editing → Dirty. Save success creates/updates the persisted checkpoint then Clean; save cancel/failure remains Dirty. Undo may return to the saved state; editing after Undo clears incompatible redo. A guarded intent adds AwaitingDecision → Saving/Discarding/Stay; execute the original intent once only.

Analysis

UnavailablePrerequisite → Ready → ReviewingParameters → Queued/Running → Completed, CompletedNoMatches, Failed or Canceled. Saving a result is a separate persistence state. A completed result whose source changed becomes OlderInput, not recomputed in place. A deleted source becomes UnavailableSource with retained snapshot when policy allows.

Sample

Inactive → ActiveSample → SampleResult. CopyReview → PersonalCopyCreated allocates new identity; a new personal analysis has a new result ID. ExitDecision → Stay or Exit preserves the separation. No sample action silently substitutes a personal record.

Search

Idle/Recent → Loading → Results, NoMatches or Failed. Scope/query changes produce a new request identity; obsolete replies cannot replace newer results. Opening a row stores its ReturnLocation; Back restores that query, scope, filters and selected record.

Registry lifecycle

Active → ArchiveReview → Archived → RestoreReview/RestoredActive. DeleteReview → ConfirmationInvalid/Valid → DependencyBlocked or Committing → Deleted or Failed. Cancel returns unchanged. Concurrent dependency changes trigger revalidation. Deleted selection is cleared and retained references use tombstones.

Notebook

Draft has saved prose and independently unsubmitted tables. SubmitRows validates/stages/persists reusable result records. SubmitReview captures revision 1 and enters InReview. ChangesRequested allows an author draft; Resubmit captures the next revision. Approved/Archived remain protected. All events are local records until a remote service exists.

Inventory

InspectWell and SelectMany are separate contexts. AssignmentDraft → Validate → OccupiedReplacementReview if needed → Commit → Updated/Failed. TransferDraft → ResolveMappings → ValidateAll → Review → CommitAll → Completed or RecoverableFailure. SnapshotCreated is immutable and does not subscribe to live-container updates.

Workflow

Keep current TaskStatus Pending/InProgress/Completed/Failed/Skipped and RequestStatus Draft/Sent. Missing mappings are explicit blockers with remedies; do not invent an unsupported Completed state for a failed mapping. Executor input resolution → step execution → output commit → cursor advance; failed commit leaves the cursor recoverable.

Automation

PipelineDraft → PublishedRevision. RunReview → Queued → Running → Completed/Failed/Canceled/PartialOutcome. CancelRequested is stage-aware. A pre-write validation failure may start a new corrected-input run. PartialOutcome requires reconciliation of written output IDs before a reviewed recovery run; never blind-retry an uncertain commit.

Bioprocess

Preserve Draft → Executing → Completed/Aborted, with explicit allowed actions and immutable execution source context. Required unit-operation completion and replicate data determine completion availability. Recipe edits do not rewrite an already planned/executing run.

Shared surface states

Each interactive control specifies default, hover, pressed, focused, disabled and busy when applicable. Each collection specifies loading, populated, first-use empty, filtered empty, failed and unavailable source. Disabled actions include the reason and remedy; routine success is non-blocking.

Scientific and input-validation contracts

Scientific and input-validation contracts

Alphabet handling

Validate source molecule before constructing a typed sequence. Retain original bytes/text, detected type, user-confirmed type and transformation report. DNA IUPAC symbols remain supported. U→T, gap removal, unsupported-residue deletion and format annotation loss require explicit review; unsupported molecule/type combinations remain recoverably blocked.

Feature coordinates

For UI start s and length n, internal start=s−1 and len=n. An inclusive UI end e gives len=e−s+1. Validate linear end ≤ sequence length. Circular wrap uses a normalized start and a length no greater than the allowed whole-molecule span. Feature-segment order and strand are preserved.

Primer/PCR

Keep existing hybridization, Tm, candidate ranking and secondary-structure calculations. A 5′ overhang is not a template-binding body. Report primer IDs, orientation, binding sites and parameter assumptions with each product; copy annotations only when requested and coordinate mapping is defined.

Digest accounting

Use domain digest outputs. For an uncut linear 12-base input ATGCGTACGTAA with EcoRI/BamHI, the expected diagnostic is no sites and one uncut 12-base molecule. Circular and linear cut cases use their respective fragment accounting; do not substitute the 18/3003 illustrative Figma fixture for computed data.

Alignment/assembly

Preserve progressive MSA, pair alignment, circular reindex mapping, strategy-specific assembly, junction primer design, Golden Gate overhang checks and combinatorial caps. Show unsupported/invalid combinations as parameter errors or no-result diagnostics with original inputs retained.

CRISPR/codon/BLAST

Keep PAM/strand scan, per-guide/off-target lists, available scores, codon host/GC/avoidance/harmonization parameters and local database selection. Display the implemented method name/version and scope. A seed-and-extend result is not claimed to be an NCBI BLAST search with equivalent statistical guarantees.

Protein/chemistry/RNA

Typed input and chain/monomer/compound references are mandatory. Report unavailable properties for unsupported chemistry rather than guessing. Show units for molecular mass, temperature, charge assumptions, titer and concentration. Preserve supported serialization round trips and source type.

Numeric validation

Parse into validated finite values; report field-local errors. Quantity/duration/volume rules are operation-specific: transfer volume must be positive and not exceed available source; empty wells may have zero quantity; division requires nonzero concentration. Avoid comparing floats for strict equality except discrete/count fields.

CSV and text export

Handle quoted commas, escaped quotes, embedded line breaks, BOM/Unicode and missing/ragged columns. Export the selected scope and actual units. Offer a clearly described spreadsheet-safe mode if formula neutralization changes text; raw scientific text must not be silently altered. The app never evaluates imported formulas.

Resource budget

Keep the UI responsive using background work, cancellation and virtualized rendering. Do not introduce an unmeasured hard sequence-size limit that removes existing capability. Proposed default: warn before eager processing of files over 64 MiB, allow a reviewed continue/cancel choice, stream records when possible and handle allocation failure recoverably. Benchmark supported sizes before declaring performance guarantees.

Acceptance, edge cases and verification strategy

Acceptance, edge cases and verification strategy

Baseline first

Run and record the existing domain/storage/appcore suites before changing behavior. The source index lists discovered tests but documentation generation does not establish that they pass. If the baseline fails, preserve evidence and resolve/triage it before attributing a failure to the UI migration.

Required commands

From repository root use cargo test -p domain; cargo test -p storage; cargo test -p appcore; cargo check -p desktop_gpui; cargo fmt --all -- --check. Run workspace-wide tests/build checks after the relevant slices pass and when the Windows/GPUI environment supports them. Record exact command, toolchain, result and revision; do not fabricate expected timings.

Identity tests

Use two records with the same display name, two store kinds with the same u64 ID, two documents with different revisions and two plates with A1. Sort/filter/reopen/delete while actions are pending. Assert the exact typed identity in every write, result and return route.

Persistence fault tests

Inject failure at temp creation, write, flush, rename, journal stage and each store commit. The last good file remains readable; false success is impossible; retry/restart cannot create duplicate outputs. Use temporary test directories and never real user config files.

Async tests

Change selection/document/revision while work runs; issue repeated Run/Cancel; close the view/app at a supported boundary; deliver an obsolete completion after a newer request. Assert captured input provenance, stage-aware cancellation and safe recovery.

Scientific fixtures

Pin domain-engine regression fixtures by molecule type, topology, coordinate convention, method and expected outputs/tolerances. Use circular wrap, no matches, ambiguous bases, primer overhangs, feature transformations, MSA reindex, assembly overhang errors, invalid SMILES/HELM and unit boundaries.

Native UI tests

Exercise text-input shortcut precedence, all clickable targets, tab order, visible focus, Escape and focus return. Inspect Windows scaling/text enlargement, high-density map labels, readable alternatives, 1280 layout and right-panel closing. Native assistive-technology exposure needs runtime inspection; a Figma frame cannot establish it.

First-user study

Observe 6–8 molecular biologists new to HelixBench performing import → interpretation → analysis → save → refind without navigation hints. Record unassisted completion, first correct control, wrong turns, identity/scope mistakes, help requests and recovery. Use the measured baseline to agree quantitative targets; a two-click count alone is not usability evidence.

Release gate

All mandatory acceptance IDs and selected edge cases pass, legacy data round trips without silent loss, no critical identity/lost-work defects remain, and all retained scientific capabilities are reachable. Unimplemented design-only features are disabled or explicitly explained rather than represented by false-success buttons.

Implementation risks, resolved policies and remaining validation

Implementation risks, resolved policies and remaining validation

Ready to implement

The authority choice, native stack, local-first scope, two-click measure, identity policy, tombstone/dependency rule, non-blocking feedback and typed-molecule routing have explicit defaults in this specification. Engineers can begin foundation tasks without another product questionnaire.

Engineering prerequisites

Before adopting proposed identity/hash/parser dependencies, verify their MSRV/license/platform compatibility with the installed Rust/GPUI build and commit Cargo.lock changes. UUID v4 generation and SHA-256 APIs were checked against primary library documentation; dependency choice is proposed, not an installed-code claim.

Scientific gate

Independent scientific-method validation is required for stronger scoring/analysis claims and new numeric behavior. Preserve existing algorithms and tests; do not “fix” scientific output to match a Figma number.

Collaboration gate

Remote reviewers, shared permissions, actual request delivery, sync and organization accounts are a separate product/backend decision. The current implementation remains local. A Reviewer A screen is a workflow fixture and must not send external messages.

Accessibility gate

The focus/error/panel patterns are specified. A native runtime review must verify semantics, screen-reader exposure, keyboard order, contrast at rendered sizes and status announcements. Do not claim WCAG conformance from Figma alone.

Prototype routing gate

Some legacy reference frames and operation-content examples remain in the Figma file. Use the normative intent/state contract and canonical frame references, not every copied reaction literally. In particular, avoid unnecessary dirty guards for read-only tools and mandatory modal success steps for routine actions.

Performance gate

No new hard maximum or latency guarantee is asserted without measurement. Capture memory, responsiveness, cancellation latency, parsing throughput and table/map scaling on declared datasets and Windows hardware before setting release performance budgets.

Document maintenance

Treat this bundle as a versioned specification. When code or Figma changes, update the source revision/hashes, feature status, canonical frame map, test results and decision log together. This snapshot does not silently track future external changes.

Journeys and state machines

Connected journeys and state machines

J-01 · First meaningful sequence result

1. Home → Import source

2. Recognized-content and transformation review

3. Open the exact sequence ID/revision

4. Choose restriction analysis with explicit scope

5. Review settings → run against captured input

6. Inspect completed/no-match/failed outcome

7. Save named output with provenance

8. Leave → find by recent work/search → reopen the same result

Owning screens: home, sequence, enzymes, history.

J-02 · Blank sequence

1. Create → enter supported DNA and topology

2. Review valid input or correct field errors

3. Create a newly identified document

4. Edit/save/analyze its own sequence

5. Refind the new document; do not return to the demo

Owning screens: home, sequence.

J-03 · Sample to personal work

1. Choose labeled sample

2. Inspect/run within sample namespace

3. Exit safely or review personal copy

4. Allocate independent document ID/revision

5. Run a new personal analysis with a new result ID

Owning screens: home, map, enzymes.

J-04 · Notebook and results

1. Create a blank entry or deliberately apply a template

2. Link a reviewed source revision

3. Write notes and add a structured table

4. Validate/submit result rows

5. Capture a submitted local-review revision

6. Record changes requested → amend draft → resubmit

7. Inspect the correct read-only submitted revision

Owning screens: notebook, registry.

J-05 · Physical sample custody

1. Choose storage/container and inspect an exact well

2. Choose a single assignment or an explicit multi-well set

3. Review existing/proposed contents and units

4. Validate source/destination transfer mappings

5. Commit a recoverable operation

6. Refresh live state and retain immutable notebook snapshots

Owning screens: inventory, notebook, registry.

J-06 · Archive, delete and retained history

1. Select exact typed record

2. Archive/review/restore using the same identity

3. For permanent delete, confirm ID and revalidate dependencies

4. Block live/unrecoverable dependencies or commit deletion

5. Clear selection and caches

6. Open retained historical result via its snapshot/tombstone

Owning screens: registry, history.

J-07 · Automation recovery

1. Review input, immutable pipeline version and output target

2. Validate parsed rows before writeback

3. Start a uniquely identified operation

4. Cancel only at a supported boundary

5. Inspect completed/failed/partial outcome

6. Reconcile retained output IDs before recovery

7. Write remaining outputs without duplication and refind by run ID

Owning screens: automation, notebook, registry.

J-08 · Source change and scientific results

1. Inspect the saved result’s captured input

2. Edit/save a newer source revision

3. Label older-input result without overwriting it

4. Review rerun inputs and allocate a new result ID

5. Compare method/parameters/outputs and export provenance

Owning screens: history, enzymes, split.

SM-IMPORT · Import review

Initial state: Idle.

States: Idle, Parsing, ReviewReady, ReviewIssues, DuplicateDecision, Committing, Opened, CommitFailed.

  • Idle → choose source → Parsing; invariant: existing work retained.
  • Parsing → recognized valid content → ReviewReady; invariant: original retained.
  • Parsing → issues → ReviewIssues; invariant: no silent cleaning.
  • ReviewIssues → correct and revalidate → ReviewReady; invariant: diff reviewed.
  • ReviewReady → matching document → DuplicateDecision; invariant: choose open/skip/copy.
  • ReviewReady → confirm selected records → Committing; invariant: typed plan.
  • Committing → persist/open succeeds → Opened; invariant: exact new IDs.
  • Committing → write fails → CommitFailed; invariant: no false success.

SM-GUARD · Unsaved navigation

Initial state: Editing.

States: Editing, Decision, Saving, SaveFailed, Continuing.

  • Editing → loss-producing intent → Decision; invariant: capture exact intent/source.
  • Decision → Stay or Escape → Editing; invariant: return invoking view.
  • Decision → Save → Saving; invariant: retain intent.
  • Saving → cancel or failure → SaveFailed; invariant: do not continue.
  • Saving → save succeeds → Continuing; invariant: perform intent once.
  • Decision → Discard → Continuing; invariant: retain saved checkpoint.

SM-ANALYSIS · Analysis/result lifecycle

Initial state: Prerequisite.

States: Prerequisite, Ready, Running, Completed, NoMatches, Failed, Canceled, Saved, OlderInput, UnavailableSource.

  • Prerequisite → valid typed input → Ready; invariant: capture scope.
  • Ready → Run → Running; invariant: immutable snapshot.
  • Running → success with matches → Completed; invariant: method/parameters retained.
  • Running → success without matches → NoMatches; invariant: not failure.
  • Running → supported cancellation → Canceled; invariant: stage truthful.
  • Completed → persist output → Saved; invariant: new result ID.
  • Saved → source changes → OlderInput; invariant: old output unchanged.
  • Saved → source deleted and snapshot retained → UnavailableSource; invariant: tombstone; no resurrection.

SM-NOTEBOOK · Local notebook review

Initial state: Draft.

States: Draft, InReview, ChangesRequested, Approved, Archived.

  • Draft → submit reviewed revision → InReview; invariant: required results persisted.
  • InReview → request changes → ChangesRequested; invariant: comment and snapshot retained.
  • ChangesRequested → resubmit next revision → InReview; invariant: same entry ID.
  • InReview → approve locally → Approved; invariant: immutable approved snapshot.
  • Approved → archive → Archived; invariant: retain historical references.

SM-RECORD · Archive and delete

Initial state: Active.

States: Active, Archived, DeleteReview, Blocked, Deleted, Failed.

  • Active → confirm archive → Archived; invariant: correct record ID.
  • Archived → restore → Active; invariant: same identity.
  • Active → request permanent delete → DeleteReview; invariant: dependencies reviewed.
  • DeleteReview → live dependency or missing snapshot → Blocked; invariant: no mutation.
  • DeleteReview → matching confirmation and valid plan → Deleted; invariant: selection cleared; tombstones retained.
  • DeleteReview → persistence fails → Failed; invariant: original retained.

SM-TRANSFER · Inventory transfer

Initial state: Draft.

States: Draft, Validated, Review, Committing, Completed, RecoverableFailure.

  • Draft → validate all mappings/units → Validated; invariant: whole ID set.
  • Validated → present impact → Review; invariant: source/destination quantities.
  • Review → confirm → Committing; invariant: journal operation.
  • Committing → all stores committed → Completed; invariant: source and destination updated.
  • Committing → interrupted/failed → RecoverableFailure; invariant: reconcile before retry.

SM-AUTOMATION · Automation run

Initial state: Reviewing.

States: Reviewing, Queued, Running, CancelRequested, Canceled, Completed, Failed, PartialOutcome, Reconciled.

  • Reviewing → validated input/target → Queued; invariant: immutable template revision.
  • Queued → start → Running; invariant: unique run ID.
  • Running → request supported cancel → CancelRequested; invariant: do not claim canceled yet.
  • CancelRequested → safe boundary reached → Canceled; invariant: written outputs explained.
  • Running → all output commits succeed → Completed; invariant: truthful row counts.
  • Running → validation fails before write → Failed; invariant: no records written.
  • Running → some outputs committed → PartialOutcome; invariant: retain output IDs.
  • PartialOutcome → reconcile journal → Reconciled; invariant: retry remaining only.

SM-SEARCH · Scoped search

Initial state: Recent.

States: Recent, Loading, Results, NoMatches, Failed.

  • Recent → query/scope changes → Loading; invariant: new request identity.
  • Loading → matching rows → Results; invariant: typed IDs.
  • Loading → no matching rows → NoMatches; invariant: source is not necessarily empty.
  • Loading → load error → Failed; invariant: query retained.
  • Results → clear query → Recent; invariant: clear explicit scope as requested.

Shared state visual references

Shared state visual references

These representative Figma captures illustrate the shared contracts. Use the state machines and screen requirements for implementation behavior; example text and data are not production defaults. The full state catalog retains frame links and authored actions.

First use

Offer an explicit sample route and an import route. Sample records must never be silently mixed into real work.

Import review

Review molecule type, records, transformations and validation before committing. Retain original input and actionable row errors.

Unsaved work guard

Save, discard or stay must act on the exact invoking draft and preserve the intended destination. Failed save keeps the guard open.

Search and recovery

Show typed results with their source context; retain the query and distinguish no matches from a load failure.

Analysis result

Show method, actual input revision, parameters, result content and explicit next actions. Saving must be truthful and refindable.

After deletion

Clear deleted selections, offer a safe next action and preserve dependency history. Undo is shown only when it can actually restore the operation.

Contextual inspection

Keep the selected well and container identity visible while showing relevant properties and actions in the right panel.

Partial operation

Distinguish committed outputs from failed or pending work. Retry only failed work without duplicating committed outputs.

Typography

Use DM Sans for interface text and Cascadia Mono for sequence/code content where used in the established design. Verify font distribution rights and availability before bundling; provide deterministic fallback metrics and validate Windows scaling. Current Home uses DM Sans Regular and Medium: 12/17, 13/19, 14/20, 15/21, 19/27, 24/34 and 27/38 (size/line-height). Heading and body roles must be named in the native theme rather than copied as scattered constants. Some labels have automatic line height; use measured frame layouts to check wrapping. Readability and accessible scaling take priority over truncating essential scientific content.

Measured shell

  • Reference frame: 1600 × 1080. Navigation: 200 wide, 16 padding, 7 item gap; rows 168 × 36 with 12 radius and 8 horizontal inset.
  • Center workspace: 1080 wide with 32 padding and 16 section gap. Header: 1016 × 62 with 12 gap. Task workspace: 1016 × 900 with 16 gap.
  • Contextual right panel: 320 wide with 24 padding and 14 section gap. Keep selection identity, relevant tools and prerequisites visible.
  • These measurements describe the reference size. At 1280 wide, follow the documented responsive states: preserve the scientific viewport and make the inspector collapsible/reopenable; do not squeeze or remove action labels without an accessible alternative.
  • Use layout containers and intrinsic text sizing. Scientific canvases may pan/zoom independently; the full application must not require horizontal scrolling to find Save or Run.

Components and states

  • Buttons: primary, secondary, quiet and destructive roles; default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled-with-reason and busy states. Primary actions use the established ink/mint/teal hierarchy. Never use a pastel color alone to communicate status.
  • Inputs: persistent label, unit or format hint, empty/value, focused, invalid, read-only and disabled states. Validation associates an exact message with the field and preserves the user value.
  • Tables: headers, sort, filter, no data, no matches, loading, failure, selection, keyboard focus and unavailable-record states. Selection and focus must remain visually distinguishable.
  • Panels: close/reopen affordance, selected-record title, relevant properties/tools, scrollable body and safe action footer. Preserve context when switching tabs or resizing.
  • Dialogs: concise title, affected object, consequences, retained draft values, explicit primary/cancel actions, focus containment and return focus. Consequential operations use the functional state machines; routine success does not block work.
  • Scientific annotations retain their semantic feature/strand/base distinctions and a legend. Decorative palette changes must not merge distinct scientific categories.
  • Semantic success/warning/error colors must be contrast-checked against their actual surface. Do not reuse an old theme token simply because its name matches. Validate text, focus and non-text control contrast before release.

Cave-art illustrations and product feedback

Retain the requested cave-painting art direction for empty, success, warning, alert and deletion illustrations: restrained charcoal/ochre figures, hand-rendered marks and light warm texture. Keep artwork secondary to the state title, explanation and next action; avoid texture behind body text or scientific data. Illustrations are decorative unless they carry information absent from the text. Loading, zero matches, failed operation, partial outcome, permissions/read-only context and true empty data need distinct copy/actions even if they share an illustration family. Use existing approved Figma artwork assets; do not substitute emoji or introduce new mascot content during implementation. Destructive confirmation names the exact target and consequence; completed deletion is a separate outcome. Respect reduced motion; essential feedback remains available without animation.

Native implementation ownership

P07 introduces reusable theme/component roles in desktop_gpui; P19 verifies keyboard, scaling, contrast, responsive behavior and large-data performance. Preserve the user-supplied HelixBench logo from Figma node 18:3 and its current v4 usage; export the approved asset and verify rendering rather than redrawing it. Document any accessibility-driven correction to a measured token with before/after evidence.

SCR-01 · Home

SCR-01 · Home

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P06.

Purpose and layout

Resume the right work or start a task without learning the navigation.

Labeled workspace navigation; Import sequence and Try a sample on first use; exact recent records and resumable work on populated Home; contextual next steps at right.

Target requirements

  • SCR-01-R1: First launch offers an empty personal workspace and an explicit sample choice. Existing installations restore their own workspace without replacing it with demo data.
  • SCR-01-R2: Recent rows resolve a typed identity or a normalized file path, never a row index or display-name match. Missing files offer Locate or Remove without altering the document.
  • SCR-01-R3: Resume a task, notebook entry or saved analysis with its selection, query, return route and persistence status. Display unsaved documents separately from saved files.
  • SCR-01-R4: Project/folder changes validate parent existence and cycles. Bulk tag/export/close operates on the reviewed ID set; canceling a dirty-document close leaves the remaining queue intact.
  • SCR-01-R5: Calendar and work totals are derived from local records; date navigation changes scope without modifying records. An empty calendar day is not a loading failure.

User flow

1. Choose a document or task

2. Resume its exact context

3. Do the work

4. Save or submit

5. Return to Home with updated status

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-01-EC1: Fresh config versus existing config with no open document.
  • SCR-01-EC2: Recent path moved, inaccessible, duplicated with different spelling, or points to a newer native-file format.
  • SCR-01-EC3: Two documents share a name; the intended stable ID must open.
  • SCR-01-EC4: One dirty document in a multi-close operation fails to save or the user cancels.
  • SCR-01-EC5: A task or entry disappears between list rendering and activation.
  • SCR-01-EC6: Sample workspace exit, personal copy and restarting the application do not merge sample and personal records.

SCR-02 · Map

SCR-02 · Map

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P08A.

Purpose and layout

Understand a construct and act directly on its sequence region.

Document identity and saved/draft state; six scientific views; editable map with zoom and readable-annotation alternative; selection-bound right tools panel.

Target requirements

  • SCR-02-R1: Map representation (Plasmid/Linear) is independent of biological topology. A display switch does not edit the molecule.
  • SCR-02-R2: All coordinates displayed to users are 1-based inclusive; internal Range remains zero-based start plus length. Circular origin-spanning selections retain ordered segments.
  • SCR-02-R3: Feature, primer and enzyme selection synchronizes the map, list and inspector. Clear selection removes dependent actions rather than retaining the previous record.
  • SCR-02-R4: Display toggles, zoom, fit, center and minimap remain available. Readable annotation lists carry the same IDs and coordinates when labels are dense.
  • SCR-02-R5: Mutating topology, origin or sequence direction has an impact preview for affected annotations/primers and remains undoable; analyses retain their captured input.

User flow

1. Open a construct

2. Select a feature or range

3. Choose a contextual action

4. Review prefilled inputs

5. Apply and return to the same map region

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-02-EC1: Empty sequence, one-base sequence, very long sequence or dense overlapping annotations.
  • SCR-02-EC2: Drag across the circular origin; reverse-strand feature; discontiguous feature segments.
  • SCR-02-EC3: Map display is Linear while topology is Circular, and the reverse.
  • SCR-02-EC4: Selection or document changes after opening a tool.
  • SCR-02-EC5: Zoom/minimap movement must not accidentally edit a feature.
  • SCR-02-EC6: Undo after a topology/origin edit restores selection and annotations; read-only display changes do not mark dirty.

Current code ownership

  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:201 — pub fn primer_from_selection(app: &mut AppState)

SCR-03 · Sequence

SCR-03 · Sequence

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P08A.

Purpose and layout

Edit bases, inspect annotations and launch analysis from the selected range.

Named sequence and version; virtualized double-stranded base rows; explicit range/strand/frame; Find bar; same contextual tools as Map.

Target requirements

  • SCR-03-R1: Paste and replacement preview the original, recognized alphabet and every meaningful transformation before mutation. Whitespace normalization is reported; unsupported symbols are not silently discarded.
  • SCR-03-R2: Editing updates affected feature/primer coordinates using the existing domain operations and preserves an undo checkpoint. Cancellation changes neither data nor dirty state.
  • SCR-03-R3: DNA/protein/name search modes stay distinct. Hit navigation, highlighting and search recents retain the query and coordinate system.
  • SCR-03-R4: Complement, six-frame translation, ORFs, genetic code and custom/history color modes preserve existing scientific behavior. Protein output is not stored as DNA.
  • SCR-03-R5: Source-view switching retains the active document, draft, range, strand, search position and scroll anchor. Clipboard failure leaves selection and content unchanged.

User flow

1. Open sequence

2. Find or select bases

3. Edit or analyze the selection

4. Validate the change

5. Save or undo without losing the position

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-03-EC1: Paste contains U, gaps, digits, Unicode, lowercase, IUPAC symbols or invalid bytes.
  • SCR-03-EC2: Replacing a region changes length or overlaps an annotation boundary.
  • SCR-03-EC3: Search has no hits, wraps to the first hit, matches the reverse strand or uses an invalid alphabet.
  • SCR-03-EC4: Cut succeeds in mutation only when required clipboard handling succeeds.
  • SCR-03-EC5: Changing the genetic code changes computed translations without corrupting annotations.
  • SCR-03-EC6: Window resizing and large text do not move the caret to an unrelated coordinate.

SCR-04 · Features

SCR-04 · Features

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P08B.

Purpose and layout

Create, verify and maintain annotations without detouring through a library.

Searchable/sortable feature table with selected-record inspector, explicit Add/Edit/Delete, detection preview and reusable feature library.

Target requirements

  • SCR-04-R1: Fields include name, kind, segments, direction, color, note, product, translation flag, genetic code, first-codon-Met option and frame offset. Preserve existing IDs when editing.
  • SCR-04-R2: Segment parsing validates linear bounds, circular spans, empty ranges and supported multi-segment syntax; show errors beside the segment input.
  • SCR-04-R3: Detect Common Features and bulk auto-annotation display candidate positions, strand, source motif and conflicts before applying a selected set.
  • SCR-04-R4: Deleting a feature is an undoable document edit. Routine completion uses an inline status or toast; it does not require a second confirmation screen.
  • SCR-04-R5: Column visibility, filters and sort do not change selection identity. A readable list is synchronized with map and sequence views.

User flow

1. Filter or select an annotation

2. Inspect its range and biological meaning

3. Edit or create

4. Validate ranges and translation

5. Save and highlight it on Map / Sequence

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-04-EC1: Duplicate names, empty name, invalid coordinates, wrapped segments and reverse-direction CDS.
  • SCR-04-EC2: Frame offset outside 0–2; partial codon; absent product; a translation flag on a noncoding feature.
  • SCR-04-EC3: Overlapping/duplicate detection candidates and ambiguous motif matches.
  • SCR-04-EC4: Library motif is empty or incompatible with the sequence alphabet.
  • SCR-04-EC5: Bulk annotation across dirty, empty and closed documents preserves per-document outcomes.
  • SCR-04-EC6: Delete the selected row after sorting; clear the inspector and keep Undo available.

  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:103 — pub fn save_feature_draft(app: &mut AppState, draft: &FeatureDraft) -> Result<(), String>

Field/draft contracts

FeatureDraft

crates/appcore/src/state.rs:199

  • id: Option<u64> — Resolve a stable typed identity from a labeled picker. Validate existence/kind at submit; do not persist a row index as a foreign key.
  • name: String — Trim for validation; require a nonempty meaningful label where the owning operation creates an object. Preserve original editable draft on error.
  • kind: String — Use a labeled finite choice with a visible selected value. Validate enum/mode availability; preserve unknown legacy values for review.
  • segments_text: String — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • direction: Direction — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • color: [u8; 3] — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • note: String — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • product: String — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • translated: bool — Explicit labeled toggle; default is specified by the owning feature. Persist only when the corresponding action is confirmed.
  • genetic_code: u8 — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • first_codon_met: bool — Explicit labeled toggle; default is specified by the owning feature. Persist only when the corresponding action is confirmed.
  • frame_offset: usize — Validate coordinate/length/frame using the owning tool; UI positions are 1-based inclusive. Reject empty/out-of-range spans and unsupported frame values.
  • error: Option<String> — System-owned validation/error state; never an editable user field.

FeatureLibDraft

crates/appcore/src/state.rs:406

  • name: String — Trim for validation; require a nonempty meaningful label where the owning operation creates an object. Preserve original editable draft on error.
  • kind: String — Use a labeled finite choice with a visible selected value. Validate enum/mode availability; preserve unknown legacy values for review.
  • motif: String — Validate the declared molecule/grammar before commit. Preserve original text and report meaningful normalization or unsupported syntax.
  • error: Option<String> — System-owned validation/error state; never an editable user field.

SCR-05 · Primers

SCR-05 · Primers

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P08C.

Purpose and layout

Design or edit an oligo, check its structure and reuse it in PCR.

Primer/pair table with binding context, length/GC/Tm/structure indicators; selected pair inspector; separate design and PCR setup/results.

Target requirements

  • SCR-05-R1: Primer sequence is entered 5′→3′ and validated using supported primer symbols; preserve phosphorylation, description and color. Display the assumed hybridization/Tm method and conditions.
  • SCR-05-R2: Design setup distinguishes the current selection anchor from the proposed amplification target. Show start, target length, target Tm, 5′ overhang and explicit forward/reverse candidate selection.
  • SCR-05-R3: Candidates include length, GC, Tm and hairpin/self-dimer indicators. An unselected or stale candidate cannot be added as an unrelated pair.
  • SCR-05-R4: PCR captures template version, both primer IDs/sequences, binding positions/directions and feature-copy policy. Open the product as a new, independently identified document.
  • SCR-05-R5: No binding or incompatible orientation is a successful diagnostic outcome, distinct from a computation error. Existing pair/primer capability remains available from the owning page within two clicks.

User flow

1. Select target or primer

2. Design or edit

3. Review Tm / GC / secondary structure

4. Save pair

5. Continue directly to PCR or assembly

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-05-EC1: Blank/invalid sequence, ambiguous binding, multiple sites and reverse-primer orientation.
  • SCR-05-EC2: Selection changes after setup; a linked primer is edited or deleted before Run.
  • SCR-05-EC3: Overhang is valid but changes the product length; primer body and overhang must be distinguished.
  • SCR-05-EC4: Target start/length exceeds a linear molecule or spans a circular origin.
  • SCR-05-EC5: No valid candidates, hairpin warning and no predicted PCR product.
  • SCR-05-EC6: Product creation with feature copy, repeated product names and canceled save retains source identity.

Field/draft contracts

PrimerDraft

crates/appcore/src/state.rs:216

  • id: Option<u64> — Resolve a stable typed identity from a labeled picker. Validate existence/kind at submit; do not persist a row index as a foreign key.
  • name: String — Trim for validation; require a nonempty meaningful label where the owning operation creates an object. Preserve original editable draft on error.
  • sequence: String — Validate the declared molecule/grammar before commit. Preserve original text and report meaningful normalization or unsupported syntax.
  • description: String — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • color: [u8; 3] — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • phosphorylated: bool — Explicit labeled toggle; default is specified by the owning feature. Persist only when the corresponding action is confirmed.
  • error: Option<String> — System-owned validation/error state; never an editable user field.

PrimerDesignDraft

crates/appcore/src/state.rs:335

  • start: String — Validate coordinate/length/frame using the owning tool; UI positions are 1-based inclusive. Reject empty/out-of-range spans and unsupported frame values.
  • len: String — Validate coordinate/length/frame using the owning tool; UI positions are 1-based inclusive. Reject empty/out-of-range spans and unsupported frame values.
  • target_tm: String — Parse finite numeric input, display units/range where relevant and apply domain-specific bounds. Do not silently substitute a default after invalid input.
  • overhang: String — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • fwd: Vec<domain::primer_design::Candidate> — Computed preview/output state. Clear or mark stale when relevant input changes; never commit an unrelated result.
  • rev: Vec<domain::primer_design::Candidate> — Computed preview/output state. Clear or mark stale when relevant input changes; never commit an unrelated result.
  • fwd_pick: usize — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • rev_pick: usize — Use the owning feature/module requirements and the current typed source definition. Optional values remain distinguishable from empty/default values; validate before commit.
  • error: Option<String> — System-owned validation/error state; never an editable user field.

PcrDraft

crates/appcore/src/state.rs:327

  • fwd: String — Current primer input is a string. The target resolves selected primer IDs to their explicit 5′→3′ sequence; never pass a display label such as T7-F as sequence bases.
  • rev: String — Current primer input is a string. The target resolves selected primer IDs to their explicit 5′→3′ sequence; never pass a display label such as T7-F as sequence bases.
  • copy_features: bool — Explicit labeled toggle; default is specified by the owning feature. Persist only when the corresponding action is confirmed.

SCR-06 · Enzymes

SCR-06 · Enzymes

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P08D.

Purpose and layout

Choose an enzyme set, inspect cut sites and simulate the digest.

Enzyme set and composable cut/region filters; cut-site table; restriction analysis setup and fragment/gel results with input provenance.

Target requirements

  • SCR-06-R1: Preserve enzyme sets, unique/double/non-cutter filters, cut counts, methylation-sensitive filtering and anywhere/selection/custom-region search.
  • SCR-06-R2: A whole-sequence digest is not silently restricted to the selected promoter. Show topology, scope, enzyme set and input revision before running.
  • SCR-06-R3: Results list fragments, lengths, cut positions and method assumptions; a gel is an additional view with a labeled ladder and migration model.
  • SCR-06-R4: Zero cut sites is a completed result. Linear and circular fragment accounting use the domain engine rather than fixed prototype values.
  • SCR-06-R5: Filter reset restores scope predictably; filtering never changes biological topology or the saved chosen-enzyme set without an explicit edit.

User flow

1. Choose enzyme set

2. Filter by experimental constraints

3. Select enzymes

4. Review cut positions

5. Open digest and gel with the chosen set

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-06-EC1: No enzyme selected, no sites, one cut in circular DNA, coincident cuts and ambiguous bases.
  • SCR-06-EC2: Custom interval is invalid, empty or wraps the origin.
  • SCR-06-EC3: A non-cutter filter combined with a region filter produces no rows.
  • SCR-06-EC4: Fragment lengths and topology-specific totals remain correct at boundary cuts.
  • SCR-06-EC5: Unknown enzyme name in an older document is reported and retained for review.
  • SCR-06-EC6: Editing the source while a digest runs creates an older-input result rather than writing into the new source context.

SCR-07 · History

SCR-07 · History

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P08D.

Purpose and layout

Understand a change and recover a previous state confidently.

Separate edit Undo/Redo history and persistent named checkpoints; current version marker; compare/restore preview; linked result provenance.

Target requirements

  • SCR-07-R1: Undo/Redo act on the current document edit stack. Named versions are persistent checkpoints and are not substitutes for Undo.
  • SCR-07-R2: Restore previews changes to sequence, features and primers and creates an intentional current state; older result provenance remains tied to the original snapshot.
  • SCR-07-R3: Use durable revision IDs instead of list indexes in persisted references. The existing 20-checkpoint retention cap cannot erase an input referenced by a retained result.
  • SCR-07-R4: Dirty-state calculation remains correct after save, undo-to-saved, redo and branching edits. Mark unsaved versions explicitly.
  • SCR-07-R5: Canceling restore leaves current state, version list and selection untouched. A failed native save does not falsely mark the document clean.

User flow

1. Choose an operation or saved version

2. Preview affected regions

3. Request revert or restore

4. Confirm scope

5. Return to the recovered document with an undo route

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-07-EC1: Undo at the first edit, redo at the last edit, branch after undo and undo back to the saved point.
  • SCR-07-EC2: Empty version list, repeated labels and restoration of an unavailable snapshot.
  • SCR-07-EC3: Pinned result input reaches the checkpoint-retention boundary.
  • SCR-07-EC4: Restore while another document is active or an analysis result is pending.
  • SCR-07-EC5: Clock changes affect timestamp ordering but not stable revision identity.
  • SCR-07-EC6: Legacy version indexes are migrated once and are never used as permanent cross-record IDs.

Current code ownership

  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:943 — pub fn save_version(app: &mut AppState, label: &str)
  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:954 — pub fn restore_version(app: &mut AppState, idx: usize)

Domain modules: crates/domain/src/document.rs.

Native presentation entry points:

  • apps/desktop_gpui/src/views/history.rs:27 — render_history
