SCR-08 · Notebook

SCR-08 · Notebook

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P11.

Purpose and layout

Capture results and move entries through review without losing work.

Entry list and document editor with blank/template choice; linked inputs; structured tables; separate text-save, table-submit and review status.

Target requirements

  • SCR-08-R1: New entries are genuinely blank. A template adds declared headings/table schemas, never unrelated measurements or a silent source link.
  • SCR-08-R2: Structured result submission validates columns, required values and source links; creates reusable results and records exactly which rows were submitted.
  • SCR-08-R3: Capture immutable submitted revisions for review. Draft edits and submitted snapshots remain distinguishable; approved/archived content is protected.
  • SCR-08-R4: Review is a local workflow in this release. Actor labels and local status recording must not imply a network message, authenticated remote reviewer or public sharing.
  • SCR-08-R5: Draft → InReview → ChangesRequested → InReview → Approved/Archived transitions retain entry ID, result IDs, source revisions, comments and revision number.
  • SCR-08-R6: Plate snapshots attached to an entry stay immutable after live inventory changes.

User flow

1. Create entry or choose template

2. Enter notes and results

3. Save draft

4. Submit or write back a table

5. Review / request changes / approve with clear status

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-08-EC1: Blank title, missing project, deleted source and invalid/ragged result rows.
  • SCR-08-EC2: Cancel template application or switch templates after writing notes.
  • SCR-08-EC3: Submit twice, amend a submitted table or persist only some of a multi-store result submission.
  • SCR-08-EC4: Request review before required results exist, reject with a comment and resubmit the same entry.
  • SCR-08-EC5: Attempt to edit an approved, archived or submitted read-only snapshot.
  • SCR-08-EC6: An automation table with 96 submitted rows and a manual table with two draft rows remain separate data groups.

Current code ownership

  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:1632 — pub fn open_notebook(app: &mut AppState)
  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:1636 — pub fn open_entry_editor(app: &mut AppState, id: Option<u64>, template: usize)
  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:1683 — pub fn save_entry(app: &mut AppState, draft: &EntryEditDraft) -> Result<u64, String>
  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:1725 — pub fn entry_action(app: &mut AppState, id: u64, action: &str)
  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:1751 — pub fn submit_entry_table(app: &mut AppState, entry_id: u64, table_idx: usize)

SCR-09 · Registry

SCR-09 · Registry

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P12.

Purpose and layout

Create, find and relate biological entities, then jump to their documents or locations.

Entity table with kind/schema and stable identity; scientific relationships; related samples; active/archived views; dependency-aware deletion.

Target requirements

  • SCR-09-R1: Preserve plasmid, strain and primer schemas; federate biologic/oligo records by typed store references instead of inventing a shared numeric ID namespace.
  • SCR-09-R2: Open, edit, archive and restore the exact selected entity after sorting or filtering. Display names are not foreign keys.
  • SCR-09-R3: Archive hides active rows but retains identity and references. Permanent delete requires exact ID confirmation and an explicit dependency summary.
  • SCR-09-R4: Block deletion when an active dependency needs a live record or a historical result lacks a durable source snapshot. Historical results with complete immutable provenance may retain a tombstone after deletion.
  • SCR-09-R5: Successful deletion clears selection, inspector actions, active-record cues and search results. Historical output cannot resurrect a deleted source through View source.
  • SCR-09-R6: CSV import reviews column mapping, row errors, duplicates and partial outcome before persisting. Relationships reject self-links and nonexistent target IDs.

User flow

1. Choose entity kind

2. Add or import

3. Validate fields and identity

4. Link document / relation / location

5. Save and verify the entity in context

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-09-EC1: Same name across kinds/stores; missing linked file; renamed document; archived reference.
  • SCR-09-EC2: Delete is canceled, ID confirmation differs, a new dependency appears or disk persistence fails.
  • SCR-09-EC3: Delete a source whose result has a snapshot versus a result whose provenance is incomplete.
  • SCR-09-EC4: Mixed valid/invalid CSV rows, duplicate headers, quoted commas and repeated import.
  • SCR-09-EC5: Deleting a row after sort/filter leaves the correct remaining selection or no selection.
  • SCR-09-EC6: Archive PR-001 must never show DNA-001 in confirmation, completion or restore.

SCR-10 · Inventory

SCR-10 · Inventory

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P13.

Purpose and layout

Locate materials and manage a selected container or plate in place.

Storage hierarchy and plate grid; separate inspect-well and bulk-selection context; assignment review; transfer mapping; immutable snapshot access.

Target requirements

  • SCR-10-R1: Scientific entity identity is distinct from physical container/sample identity. Store typed entity references, container IDs and explicit quantity/concentration units.
  • SCR-10-R2: A well control carries its own plate ID and coordinate; bulk assignment carries the complete reviewed set of well IDs. Row indexes and a fixed A1–A4 string are not action payloads.
  • SCR-10-R3: Assignment reviews previous contents, proposed entity, role and quantity; occupied wells require explicit replacement review.
  • SCR-10-R4: Transfer validates all source volumes, destination occupancy, units and mappings before committing the entire reviewed operation. Source subtraction, destination addition and audit use a recoverable persistence boundary.
  • SCR-10-R5: Refreshing or returning from an operation updates occupancy, counts, selected-well details and filters. Earlier notebook snapshots do not change.
  • SCR-10-R6: Validate storage parent/cycle rules and plate dimensions; barcode keyboard input/paste is lookup data, not evidence of camera/scanner integration.

User flow

1. Select location / container

2. Inspect contents or plate

3. Add or assign material

4. Validate quantity / placement

5. Save or snapshot into a notebook entry

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-10-EC1: Empty and occupied wells, A1/H12 boundaries, another plate with the same coordinate, empty selection and bulk selection.
  • SCR-10-EC2: Negative, zero, nonfinite quantity; missing legacy concentration unit; incompatible mass/volume units.
  • SCR-10-EC3: Destination is occupied, source equals destination, duplicate destinations or source volume is insufficient.
  • SCR-10-EC4: One of four reviewed transfers fails before commit or persistence fails after staging.
  • SCR-10-EC5: A storage node is moved into its own descendant or a selected container is deleted.
  • SCR-10-EC6: Live updates leave immutable experiment snapshots unchanged; inspect-well does not silently alter the bulk selected set.

SCR-11 · Workflows

SCR-11 · Workflows

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P14.

Purpose and layout

Know what to do next, execute it, and submit an explicit result.

Named tasks/requests and flowchart; selected task details, required inputs, output mapping, blocker and next executable step.

Target requirements

  • SCR-11-R1: Every row opens its own task or request ID and current status. Assignee, due date and source references remain visible.
  • SCR-11-R2: A task with missing required mappings is blocked with a field-level remedy; repairing it does not silently execute the next step.
  • SCR-11-R3: Request draft/sent and task execution status are distinct local state machines. Send records a local transition, not a remote delivery.
  • SCR-11-R4: Execute a reviewed graph step against captured inputs; advance only after its outputs persist successfully. Reject missing steps, cycles or incompatible output types.
  • SCR-11-R5: Resume retains the run cursor, selected task and mapping; cancellation or failed writeback does not skip or duplicate a step.

User flow

1. Choose task or request

2. Inspect required input

3. Start work

4. Enter output and complete or fail

5. See next step and audit event

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-11-EC1: Missing/deleted input, invalid mapping key, duplicate task title, no selected task and inconsistent assignee label.
  • SCR-11-EC2: A downstream mapping fails after an upstream step succeeds.
  • SCR-11-EC3: Repeated Execute, status edit during execution and a completed step invoked again.
  • SCR-11-EC4: Malformed flowchart, dangling edge, branch with no output or a cycle.
  • SCR-11-EC5: Request validation fails or local persistence fails after Send is selected.
  • SCR-11-EC6: Returning from Notebook or Registry restores the same task rather than opening a generic worklist.

SCR-12 · Insights

SCR-12 · Insights

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P15.

Purpose and layout

Build a useful view of workspace data and export exactly what is shown.

Local dashboard blocks with visible source scope, grouping/filter parameters, chart/table alternatives, refresh status and CSV export.

Target requirements

  • SCR-12-R1: Identify the underlying dataset and its local scope before interpreting a block. Display the query/grouping/filter assumptions and refresh timestamp.
  • SCR-12-R2: Distinguish no source records, no matching filtered rows, a missing parameter, query failure and unavailable source references.
  • SCR-12-R3: Chart axes, units and category legends are labeled. Offer a readable data table and stable-ID links back to the contributing records.
  • SCR-12-R4: Parameters and dataset revision form the cache key; changing a filter or source invalidates stale aggregates without replacing a different block.
  • SCR-12-R5: CSV export uses the displayed scope, correct quoting and an explicit local destination; cancellation or failed write does not report export success.

User flow

1. Add insight

2. Choose dataset and grouping

3. Preview chart

4. Save the dashboard state

5. Export the named source or displayed result

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-12-EC1: Empty dataset, a category with no values, missing numeric values and nonfinite input.
  • SCR-12-EC2: Filter excludes all rows; selected grouping column no longer exists.
  • SCR-12-EC3: Source records change while aggregation runs.
  • SCR-12-EC4: Long labels, many categories and horizontal scrolling at smaller widths.
  • SCR-12-EC5: Dataset is local but a referenced source file is inaccessible or deleted.
  • SCR-12-EC6: CSV contains commas, quotes, newlines, Unicode and values that spreadsheet applications interpret as formulas.

Current code ownership

  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:2799 — pub fn datasets(app: &AppState) -> Vec<domain::insights::Dataset>
  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:2862 — pub fn insights_add_block( app: &mut AppState, name: &str, source: &str, chart: domain::insights::Chart, group_by: Option<String>, )
  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:2879 — pub fn insights_export(app: &mut AppState, source: &str)

Domain modules: crates/domain/src/insights.rs.

Native presentation entry points:

  • apps/desktop_gpui/src/lab.rs:808 — render_insights

Use the typed domain/store models in the data reference and the proposed request/operation models. No nonexistent UI draft is assumed.

SCR-13 · Automation

SCR-13 · Automation

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P16.

Purpose and layout

Run an explicit pipeline against an explicit file, with traceable output.

Draft/published pipeline configuration; input review and mapping; run history by ID; running/cancel/recovery states; output and writeback audit.

Target requirements

  • SCR-13-R1: Published configurations have an immutable revision reference. Editing a draft does not mutate an in-flight run or an earlier completed run.
  • SCR-13-R2: CSV ingestion handles quoting, newlines, encoding and row shape. Validate required identifiers and mapping before any writeback.
  • SCR-13-R3: Running, cancel-requested, canceled, completed, failed and partial-write outcomes are distinct. Do not present a Cancel action when the actual stage cannot safely support it.
  • SCR-13-R4: Persist run IDs, source fingerprint, parameters, staged outputs and per-row writeback identities. A retry cannot repeat successful output writes.
  • SCR-13-R5: Recovery of a validation-only failure starts a reviewed new run. Recovery of a partial write first reconciles retained output IDs and the remaining row set.
  • SCR-13-R6: An output table and linked notebook keep submitted automation rows separate from existing manual draft rows.

User flow

1. Select pipeline

2. Load CSV and validate columns

3. Review transform and writeback destination

4. Publish if required

5. Run selected pipeline

6. Inspect outcome and records written

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-13-EC1: Empty/malformed CSV, duplicate headers, missing row IDs, quoted commas/newlines, UTF-8 BOM and repeated source input.
  • SCR-13-EC2: Template deleted/unpublished after review; unknown pipeline step; changed destination schema.
  • SCR-13-EC3: Cancel during parsing, before commit or after some writes; application closes during a run.
  • SCR-13-EC4: Persistence succeeds for outputs but not run history/audit; restart must reconcile the journal.
  • SCR-13-EC5: Double-click Start, retry an already completed run or resume an uncertain partial outcome.
  • SCR-13-EC6: R-017 and R-018 remain distinct run details; no history row opens another run just because it shares a pipeline.

SCR-14 · Split

SCR-14 · Split

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P10A.

Purpose and layout

Compare two known documents while preserving their identities and selections.

Two named inputs with active-pane indication; independent/synchronized navigation; pair/multiple alignment setup and saved alignments.

Target requirements

  • SCR-14-R1: Each pane identifies document ID, revision, topology and active selection. Tool actions specify the pane or the captured input set.
  • SCR-14-R2: Choosing another input honors its dirty-document guard and keeps the other pane intact. The same document in both panes is an explicit choice.
  • SCR-14-R3: Alignment captures pair order, reindex option, scoring/method and source versions; saved alignments have their own stable ID.
  • SCR-14-R4: Preserve existing pair and progressive multiple alignment, consensus and identity outputs; do not turn a display comparison into sequence mutation.
  • SCR-14-R5: Opening a saved result whose source is closed or deleted shows retained provenance and offers a safe source-resolution path.

User flow

1. Choose two documents

2. Compare their representations

3. Select a region or discrepancy

4. Open in editor or align

5. Return with both choices preserved

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-14-EC1: No second document, same input twice, one empty input, linear versus circular and reversed input order.
  • SCR-14-EC2: Selection is made in the right pane but a tool tries to use the left pane.
  • SCR-14-EC3: Circular auto-reindex changes coordinate presentation; preserve an explicit mapping.
  • SCR-14-EC4: Source edited during a long alignment or removed while loading a saved alignment.
  • SCR-14-EC5: Very long sequences or many documents require budget review, background work and cancellation.
  • SCR-14-EC6: Delete a saved alignment after sorting; retain the underlying documents.

  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:839 — pub fn open_alignment(app: &mut AppState)
  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:849 — pub fn run_alignment(app: &mut AppState, draft: &mut AlignmentDraft)
  • crates/appcore/src/actions.rs:891 — pub fn alignment_save(app: &mut AppState, name: &str)

crates/appcore/src/state.rs:348

SCR-15 · Biologics

SCR-15 · Biologics

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P17.

Purpose and layout

Register a protein entity and inspect its chains, domains and numbering.

Biologic identity/format with chain selection, components and numbering; explicit protein-input analysis; related record/sample links.

Target requirements

  • SCR-15-R1: Fields preserve name, format, numbering and all chains. Chain identity, sequence type and length remain explicit across tools.
  • SCR-15-R2: Protein analysis consumes the selected protein or an explicitly reviewed translation product. A DNA document cannot silently become HC-014.
  • SCR-15-R3: Display molecular properties and alignment with method/units/assumptions; save a result linked to the actual protein chain revision.
  • SCR-15-R4: A numbering/annotation scheme is labeled by the implementation actually present; unsupported regions or formats remain visible as limitations.
  • SCR-15-R5: Deleting or editing a chain reviews dependent biologic/result links and preserves immutable historical input.

User flow

1. Register entity and format

2. Validate chains and numbering

3. Select entity

4. Inspect domains/numbered residues

5. Continue to protein analysis

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-15-EC1: Missing chain, unsupported amino acid, stop/gap symbols, unusual chain length and duplicate names.
  • SCR-15-EC2: Selected light chain differs from the default heavy chain; never substitute another chain.
  • SCR-15-EC3: Biologic format expects a chain that is missing or cannot be classified.
  • SCR-15-EC4: Protein comparison is blank, invalid or the wrong molecular type.
  • SCR-15-EC5: Numbering scheme cannot assign a residue; do not invent coverage.
  • SCR-15-EC6: A chain changes after analysis setup; historical property results retain their captured source.

SCR-16 · Chemistry

SCR-16 · Chemistry

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P17.

Purpose and layout

Register a compound, inspect its structure and manage reactions or material lots.

Compound list and supported-SMILES inspection; substructure search; reaction identities/equivalents; salt/solvate forms and physical material lots.

Target requirements

  • SCR-16-R1: Validate the supported SMILES subset before deriving formula/mass. Unsupported stereochemistry or syntax is not silently interpreted as a fully supported structure.
  • SCR-16-R2: Separate compound identity, reaction identity and material-lot quantity/location. Use stable IDs for reaction participants and form references.
  • SCR-16-R3: Reaction input identifies reactant/product and positive finite equivalents; calculated changes show the assumptions of the local model.
  • SCR-16-R4: Substructure search uses the implemented matching semantics and shows no-match independently from parse failure.
  • SCR-16-R5: Compound/reaction deletion checks references. Repeated display names and a changed selected row cannot redirect a save/delete to another compound.

User flow

1. Add compound by SMILES

2. Validate structure/properties

3. Select compound

4. Add lot or define reaction

5. Save and inspect linked result

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-16-EC1: Unbalanced ring/branch/bracket syntax, unsupported element/bond/stereochemistry and malformed charge.
  • SCR-16-EC2: Zero/negative/nonfinite equivalents or missing participant.
  • SCR-16-EC3: Compound is referenced by a reaction, lot, registry relation or result.
  • SCR-16-EC4: A salt/solvate form changes molecular mass while a lot retains its own quantity unit.
  • SCR-16-EC5: Substructure query fails to parse or matches no compounds.
  • SCR-16-EC6: Formula/mass computation is unavailable for an unsupported structure; never display a fabricated number.

SCR-17 · RNA / Oligos

SCR-17 · RNA / Oligos

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P17.

Purpose and layout

Create a modified oligo, inspect HELM and apply an explicit modification pattern.

Named RNA/modified-oligo list; direction, sequence, chemistry pattern and monomer inspection; HELM import/export and related identity.

Target requirements

  • SCR-17-R1: Validate RNA/oligo input using its own alphabet and modification model; never pass it through DNA cleaning without explicit conversion review.
  • SCR-17-R2: Preserve name, sequence, selected pattern, modification code and HELM source. Show the modified positions before applying a pattern.
  • SCR-17-R3: Sequence order, direction and terminal chemistry remain explicit. Properties reflect the selected oligo, not a generic example.
  • SCR-17-R4: HELM parsing reports unsupported monomers/connections and preserves original text for correction; export describes supported coverage.
  • SCR-17-R5: Delete/edit reviews dependent references and retains historical result provenance.

User flow

1. Add RNA or HELM input

2. Choose modification pattern

3. Validate the oligo

4. Inspect sequence/MW/GC

5. Apply or revise modifications and keep a clear change summary

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-17-EC1: Mixed T/U, DNA pasted as RNA, unsupported monomer, terminal modification and empty sequence.
  • SCR-17-EC2: HELM record has malformed syntax or a monomer outside the local library.
  • SCR-17-EC3: A modification pattern targets a missing position or conflicts with existing chemistry.
  • SCR-17-EC4: Same name with different chemistry or an edited oligo still selected by row index.
  • SCR-17-EC5: No property model exists for a chosen modification; show unavailable rather than a guessed value.
  • SCR-17-EC6: Round-trip supported HELM without changing residue order or chemistry.

RnaDraft

SCR-18 · In Vivo

SCR-18 · In Vivo

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P18.

Purpose and layout

Track a study, add measurements and understand cohort context.

Study identity/species/strain; animals and cohorts; measurement timeline; explicit-unit calculation helper; study schedule and exports.

Target requirements

  • SCR-18-R1: Keep study and animal IDs distinct. Measurements bind to the selected animal and date/day, not the currently highlighted row after a filter.
  • SCR-18-R2: Weight and measurement units are visible. Numeric inputs must be finite and compatible with the domain model; conversions are explicit.
  • SCR-18-R3: Cohort randomization captures seed, group count and the animal set; preview imbalance and avoid silently re-randomizing an established assignment.
  • SCR-18-R4: The calculation helper displays formula, input units and output units and remains a calculation aid; no treatment recommendation is inferred from a prototype fixture.
  • SCR-18-R5: Study deletion reviews animals, measurements and downstream references; canceled or failed persistence retains the existing study.

User flow

1. Create/select study

2. Add animals

3. Review cohorts and planned measurements

4. Record measurements

5. Inspect welfare and trends

6. Review calculation inputs and result

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-18-EC1: No study/animal selected, duplicate animal tag within a study, missing species and deleted study.
  • SCR-18-EC2: Negative/nonfinite weight or measurement; missing unit; duplicate day entries.
  • SCR-18-EC3: Group count exceeds animal count, empty cohort, unequal groups and repeated randomization with the same seed.
  • SCR-18-EC4: Concentration is zero or units are incompatible in the calculation helper.
  • SCR-18-EC5: A measurement edit occurs after a cohort summary was computed.
  • SCR-18-EC6: Export includes animal/study IDs and units without conflating identical tags in different studies.

SCR-19 · Bioprocess

SCR-19 · Bioprocess

Current Figma screen · Implementation phase P18.

Purpose and layout

Plan the correct recipe run, follow operations and compare replicates.

Recipe/unit-operation definition; draft/executing/completed/aborted runs; operator steps; replicate conditions/titer and cross-run comparison.

Target requirements

  • SCR-19-R1: Recipe identity and an execution run are different objects. Capture the recipe revision and input lots when a run starts.
  • SCR-19-R2: Start, complete, abort and step-completion actions obey the domain state machine; a completed/aborted run cannot silently restart.
  • SCR-19-R3: Durations, conditions, titer and quantities have visible units and finite values. Preserve the selected run/replicate during editing.
  • SCR-19-R4: Comparison identifies every run, recipe, replicate and condition rather than displaying unlabeled aggregate values.
  • SCR-19-R5: Deleting a run or recipe reviews dependent records; physical lot consumption and result recording use recoverable operation boundaries when implemented.

User flow

1. Choose recipe

2. Plan a named run

3. Start run

4. Complete operations and enter replicates

5. Review results

6. Complete or abort with a clear audit trail

Use the shared typed context, validation/review, persistence and return-location contracts at every relevant transition. Prototype fixture IDs and figures are never production defaults.

States and recovery

  • Loading: retain prior context and identify the active request/operation.
  • Populated: show stable object identity, meaningful status and available actions.
  • No data: offer the relevant creation/import action.
  • No matches: retain query/scope and expose Reset or Change settings.
  • Invalid prerequisite: explain the missing input and provide its remedy.
  • Validation/write failure: retain draft values and show a constructive correction/retry.
  • Dirty/partial/stale/unavailable states use the shared state machines when applicable.

Screen-specific edge cases

  • SCR-19-EC1: No recipe selected, no unit operations, empty name/product and a recipe changed after run planning.
  • SCR-19-EC2: Start twice, complete with incomplete required steps, abort at a boundary or toggle a step in a locked run.
  • SCR-19-EC3: Negative/nonfinite duration or titer and mixed condition units.
  • SCR-19-EC4: Duplicate replicate labels and comparison of incompatible process/measurement units.
  • SCR-19-EC5: Run deletion while a computation or comparison is open.
  • SCR-19-EC6: Restart after a partially persisted operation retains run identity and does not silently consume lots twice.

Step-by-step implementation

HelixBench UX v4 Implementation Plan

> For agentic workers: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Do not delegate without user authorization. Steps use checkbox tracking.

Goal: Implement UX v4 while preserving every existing scientific capability and local-data compatibility.

Architecture: Retain Rust domain → appcore/storage → GPUI boundaries. Add typed identity/context and durable operation/result contracts before wiring the new shell and module workflows. Algorithms remain headless and keep their regression fixtures.

Tech Stack: Rust 2021; GPUI 0.2.2 from the inspected workspace; serde/serde_json local versioned files.

Spec: This bundle README.md and chapters 01–09; canonical repository path docs/implementation-ux-v4/README.md.

Global constraints

  • Every command carries stable source/target IDs and relevant revision IDs. Never bind a mutation to a display name, row index or currently active record at completion time.
  • UI coordinates are 1-based inclusive. Domain Range is zero-based start plus length, with documented circular wrap. Conversions occur at a typed boundary and are tested once.
  • Keep original import/paste text and produce a transformation report before meaningful changes. Invalid input cannot silently disappear.
  • A protein tool cannot choose a chain because DNA is active; a well cannot become A1 because H12 was clicked; no selection yields a prerequisite state.
  • View switches retain the same draft. Destructive replacement, document close, file open and app close guard dirty data. Save failure/cancel never performs the pending intent.
  • The UI reports saved/submitted/deleted only after the required persistence boundary succeeds. Partial/uncertain outcomes are not called success.
  • Result, submitted-entry and plate-snapshot provenance is immutable. New source edits do not rewrite old outputs.
  • Deleting a selection clears its inspector and actions. Filters/sorts retain the selected ID or explicitly clear it; they never select an unrelated row silently.
  • Each job has an operation ID and captured inputs. Closing a view does not retarget its completion; stale results remain tied to their captured source.
  • The local application does not claim remote delivery, authenticated review or cloud synchronization without an implemented service.
  • Multi-record and cross-store actions validate a complete plan, commit predictably, and reconcile on restart without repeating successful writes.
  • Visible labels, focus, keyboard navigation, readable scientific alternatives and announced status are part of the interaction, not optional decoration.

Review focus

  • Same-name/cross-store IDs must never retarget an action — P01/P02/P12.
  • Lossy or wrong-molecule import must retain original input — P03.
  • Ignored persistence failure or a retry must never create false success/duplicate output — P04/P13/P16.
  • A source revision or submitted snapshot must not change behind a result/reviewer — P01/P09/P11.
  • Keyboard/text editing, 1280 layout and large scientific data must remain operable — P07/P19.

Suggested new-file responsibilities

  • crates/domain/src/identity.rs — owned by P01: Stable identity, revision provenance and migrations.
  • crates/domain/src/results.rs — owned by P01: Stable identity, revision provenance and migrations.
  • crates/storage/src/migrations.rs — owned by P01: Stable identity, revision provenance and migrations.
  • crates/storage/src/results.rs — owned by P01: Stable identity, revision provenance and migrations.
  • crates/appcore/src/navigation.rs — owned by P02: Navigation intents, selection and dirty-work guards.
  • crates/appcore/src/import.rs — owned by P03: Safe import interpretation and commit.
  • crates/domain/src/operation.rs — owned by P04: Operation controller, persistence errors and feedback.
  • crates/appcore/src/operations.rs — owned by P04: Operation controller, persistence errors and feedback.
  • crates/storage/src/operations.rs — owned by P04: Operation controller, persistence errors and feedback.
  • crates/appcore/src/commands.rs — owned by P05: Command registry and scoped workspace search.
  • crates/appcore/src/workspace_search.rs — owned by P05: Command registry and scoped workspace search.
  • crates/appcore/src/first_use.rs — owned by P06: First-use Home, samples and resume.
  • crates/appcore/src/results.rs — owned by P09: Saved analysis result lifecycle.
  • apps/desktop_gpui/src/views/results.rs — owned by P09: Saved analysis result lifecycle.
  • crates/appcore/src/record_refs.rs — owned by P12: Typed Registry, relationships and deletion.
  • crates/appcore/src/inventory_ops.rs — owned by P13: Inventory assignment, transfer and snapshots.
  • crates/storage/src/csv.rs — owned by P16: Automation targets, journals and recovery.
  • crates/appcore/src/automation_ops.rs — owned by P16: Automation targets, journals and recovery.

Tasks are ordered by dependency. Each task is a reviewable slice, not a promise of a fixed duration. Domain/API behavior precedes UI bindings. Proposed test names below are new tests to write; they are not baseline test results.

P00 · Baseline and scientific regression inventory

Goal: Record the current command/test baseline and golden scientific fixtures without changing production behavior.

Prerequisites: None; read the baseline and authority chapters first.

Files:

  • Modify/review: crates/domain/src
  • Modify/review: crates/storage/src
  • Modify/review: crates/appcore/src
  • Modify/review: apps/desktop_gpui/src
  • Create tests: crates/appcore/tests/ux_v4_p00.rs

Interfaces:

  • Consumes: Inspected repository and specification evidence.
  • Produces: Existing scientific fixtures, source manifest and recorded baseline results.

Required tests:

  • baseline_existing_suites
  • legacy_native_round_trip
  • Step 1: Read the owning screen/feature/state contracts and the cited current APIs; record any newly discovered contradiction before changing scientific behavior.
  • Step 2: Add the listed behavior tests and representative valid/invalid/cancel/stale-ID fixtures in the proposed test file. Confirm the new expectation fails for the intended reason; P00 instead records the existing baseline.
  • Step 3: Run cargo test -p domain, cargo test -p storage, cargo test -p appcore and cargo check -p desktop_gpui; record actual baseline results. A new failing behavior test is not required for this read-only baseline task.
  • Step 4: Implement the minimal domain/storage/appcore contract and error propagation before wiring its GPUI controls. Reuse the current algorithm entry points; no fixture ID or result value may become a production default.
  • Step 5: Wire the UI states, prerequisites, labeled entry point and return context. Validate the success path plus the task-specific edge conditions and one persistence/cancel failure.
  • Step 6: Re-run the focused tests, cargo test -p appcore and cargo check -p desktop_gpui for changed bindings; run formatting and relevant scientific regression suites. Record actual outputs and update feature status.
  • Step 7: Review the diff against the acceptance IDs, stage only this task’s files and create a local checkpoint commit after checks pass. Publishing or external delivery follows the user’s authorization.

Completion gate: Existing scientific fixtures, source manifest and recorded baseline results. The listed tests pass and the owning feature traceability entries include implementation/test evidence.

ST-277 · Feedback / Pattern guidance

Reference or alternate fixture · 1600 × 410 · Open Figma frame

Displayed content

  • Use feedback that matches the consequence
  • Success: confirm the completed action without interrupting work. Keep links to its result.
  • Warning: describe the risk before proceeding and offer a safe way back.
  • Alert: identify the affected record or field, preserve recoverable input, and give a repair action.
  • Delete: identify the object, show dependency impact, and distinguish archiving from permanent deletion.
  • Implementation handoff: announce success without stealing focus; keep important errors visible. Dialogs need keyboard focus management, a named heading, a safe initial focus and return focus. Never rely on color or artwork alone.
  • Examples use illustrative records. Archive/restore and permanent-delete behavior are proposed contracts and require capability checks in the implementation.

Authored actions

[]

ST-575 · Flow completion / Interaction contracts

Linked functional state · 1600 × 1080 · Open Figma frame

Displayed content

  • Interaction and accessibility contracts
  • Implementation handoff · required behavior beyond static frames
  • Search
  • New
  • Selection and record context
  • Keep document ID/version, selected range, strand and selected wells through every tool and output.
  • Panels and dialogs
  • Name the panel; provide close and Escape; define modal versus non-modal behavior.
  • Modal: move focus inside, contain its tab order, keep the background inert, and return focus to the invoking control. Non-modal: allow a deliberate return to the workspace.
  • Validation, status and recovery
  • Associate errors with fields, retain input, announce status changes, and preserve a safe cancellation path.
  • Scientific and persistence checks
  • Validate algorithms, units, parsing, provenance, file export, cancellation and duplicate detection in implementation.
  • Focus and field validation
  • Visible focus and adjacent correction messages are specified for implementation.
  • Sequence name
  • Expression fragment
  • Keyboard focus remains visible until focus moves.
  • Sequence input
  • ATG?GTACGTAA
  • Position 4: replace “?” with a supported base.
  • Context & next steps
  • These contracts require runtime and accessibility verification. Native prototype links alone do not establish conformance.
